claim: LT2 replaces softmax attention inside a weight-tied looped Transformer with linear or sparse attention; LT2-sparse is the sparse arm
quote: We study two variants: LT2-linear with linear attention and LT2-sparse with sparse attention.
notes: Closest Transformer-vocabulary hit: a looped Transformer with learned sparse (top-w) attention compared against a dense looped Transformer.

claim: LT2 sparse mixers include NSA (top-w selected indices) and DSA (top-w selected by a lightning indexer), i.e. learned content-based top-k over the causal context
quote: KV cache + compressed blocks; ℐ t : top- w selected indices
notes: Selection is block/token top-w over all previous tokens (causal LM), learned end-to-end; whether DSA indexer gets an auxiliary/distillation loss in LT2 is not stated in the text we read.

claim: LT2 looped variants define a Looped Transformer as N shared blocks reused for T iterations
quote: yielding effective depth T ⋅ N with only N unique parameter sets—a T × parameter reduction over a Transformer of equivalent depth.

claim: LT2 synthetic state-tracking+recall task grows n=m along a curriculum and reports the largest stage solved (n_max), i.e. trained-at-size performance, not train-small/test-large extrapolation
quote: We tie n = m and grow them together along the curriculum { 8 , 16 , 32 , 64 , 128 , 256 } ; a model advances once eval accuracy reaches 0.90 within a 100 k-step budget.
notes: Models are trained at each stage before being scored there; this is a capacity/learnability measure, not size extrapolation.

claim: On LT2 state-tracking+recall, the dense Looped Transformer plateaus at n_max=64 at every loop count T
quote: Looped Transformer and Looped Full+Window plateau at stage 4 ( n max = 64 ) and never reach stage 5 at any T .
notes: 4-layer 256-wide backbone; dense arm = softmax looped Transformer.

claim: On LT2 state-tracking+recall, Looped NSA (learned top-k sparse attention in a loop) reaches n_max=128, double the dense looped Transformer
quote: three subquadratic variants — Looped NSA, Looped GDN+Window, and Looped GDN+NSA — all reach stage 5 ( n max = 128 )
notes: Nearest published evidence that learned sparse routing inside a loop beats a dense looped Transformer on a synthetic task. Not size extrapolation; no sharpened (entmax) arm; single-number outcome, seeds not stated in the sentence.

claim: LT2 compares sparse and dense looped arms at the same parameter budget
quote: a doubling of n max over the global-attention baseline at the same parameter budget.
notes: Parameter-matched; FLOPs not matched (sparse arms spend fewer attention FLOPs per loop).

claim: LT2 language-model comparisons hold loop count T=4 and parameter count fixed across variants
quote: All variants use T = 4 at matched parameter count.
notes: Equal steps + equal params; FLOP matching not claimed.

claim: In LT2, sparse looped variants train without loss spikes but end at slightly higher LM loss than the dense looped Transformer
quote: Sparse looped variants train without the spikes seen in the full-attention loop, but reach a slightly higher final loss than the Looped Transformer.
notes: LM pretraining at 0.6B/1.3B on FineWeb-Edu.

claim: In LT2 NIAH-Single-1 at 4096 tokens (trained at 2048), the dense Looped Transformer scores 0.0
notes: Columns: SWDE SQD FDA TQA NQ DROP then NIAH-S1 at 1024/2048/4096; column assignment read from the flattened table.

claim: In LT2 NIAH-Single-1 at 4096 tokens, Looped Hybrid (GDN+DSA) scores 91.4 vs 0.0 for the dense looped Transformer
notes: Length extrapolation 2x on retrieval, but the sparse arm is confounded with a linear-attention (GDN) branch; no pure looped-sparse row in Table 5; LM-scale, not algorithmic size extrapolation.

claim: LT2 attributes better NIAH extrapolation to the GDN+DSA loop despite it having no quadratic component
quote: Looped Hybrid (GDN+DSA) tracks the Looped Transformer closely on the knowledge suite despite containing no quadratic component, and additionally extrapolates substantially better at NIAH-4096.

claim: Looped Transformers on graph walks: the hidden state steers which transition a frozen shared loop performs, with attention routing as a causal pathway
quote: Together, these results show that the hidden state can control shared computation, with attention routing as a causal pathway.
notes: Interpretability study of dense-softmax looped models; no sparse/top-k arm, no architecture comparison.

claim: In native looped-Transformer trajectories, a loop can advance by different numbers of graph steps
quote: showing that recurrent progress need not follow a fixed one-loop-one-step pattern.
notes: Relevant to our step-budget design (D3): one loop ≠ one hop in learned dense loops.

claim: Wu et al. vary intermediate supervision across five matched pairs of graph-walk looped models
quote: Across five matched pairs of graph models, changing intermediate supervision during backbone training changes which transitions can induce.

claim: In recurrent-depth LMs, attention routing (support and distribution) stabilises across loops earlier than hidden states
quote: the model first discovers a sparse working set of relevant context and then continues refining representations over largely the same routing support.
notes: Empirical support that dense looped attention becomes effectively sparse and stable across steps; argues that per-step re-routing may be redundant late in the loop.

claim: WISE is training-free: global attention in early loops discovers a block working set that later loops reuse as routing support
quote: a training-free method that uses unrestricted global attention during early recurrent steps to discover a block-structured working set, and then reuses it as the routing support in later steps
notes: Inference-time sparsification of a pretrained dense looped LM; no trained routing, no extrapolation on algorithmic tasks.

claim: WISE is evaluated on multi-hop QA against full-attention inference
quote: Across multi-hop QA benchmarks, WISE largely preserves the behavior of full-attention inference

claim: MoSA: each attention head selects its own k tokens by expert-choice routing (learned content-based top-k over all tokens)
quote: where each attention head is treated like an expert and selects its own specific tokens from the input.
notes: Not looped/weight-tied; LM only; no length or size extrapolation. Already-known Routing Transformer is its baseline.

claim: MoSA reports up to 27% better perplexity than dense attention at identical compute
quote: MoSA is the only one that can outperform the dense baseline, sometimes with up to 27% better perplexity for an identical compute budget.
notes: IsoFLOP comparison, non-looped. Shows learned top-k routing can beat dense at equal FLOPs in LM.

claim: MoSA reduces per-head complexity from O(T^2) to O(k^2+T)
quote: By selecting k tokens from a sequence of length T , MoSA reduces the computational complexity of each attention head from O ⁡ ( T 2 ) to O ⁡ ( k 2 + T ) .
notes: Expert-choice: tokens are chosen by heads, not keys by queries — differs from per-query top-k.

claim: UniMatrix is a Universal-Transformer-style family reusing a shared recurrent block across depth
quote: We introduce UniMatrix , a Universal Transformer style family that reuses a shared recurrent block across depth and augments it with hybrid state updates

claim: UniMatrix-SparsePointer (sparse slot routing + pointer-logit fusion) reaches 99.2% on synthetic associative recall
quote: UniMatrix-SparsePointer , which adds sparse slot routing and direct pointer-logit fusion, reaches 75.6% on the original pilot recipe and 99.2% on a no-dropout follow-up
notes: Pilot study; baseline is a non-looped Transformer (25.4%); no looped dense baseline, no sharpened baseline, no length/size extrapolation.

claim: ChainGPT (ICLR 2026) combines recurrent depth with state-guided sparse attention
locator: Abstract (ML Anthology mirror of ICLR 2026 paper)
quote: Within each layer, ChainGPT employs multi-substep state updates combined with state-guided sparse attention, enabling deep local computation and efficient long-range modeling without quadratic costs.
notes: LM/reasoning model; abstract gives no size/length extrapolation or looped-dense vs sharpened comparison.

claim: ChainGPT full text (OpenReview kdZbxizwGK) not retrieved: OpenReview browser-verification challenge
notes: Secondary summaries say SGSA = sliding window + periodic anchors (fixed pattern, not learned top-k); unverified at primary source.

claim: Graph Machine constructs and revises relational edges across layers via edge-augmented attention and edge-centric referral
quote: this enables the model to dynamically and differentiably construct and revise relational graphs across layers.
notes: State-conditioned learned graph rebuilt per layer; soft (temperature-sharpened) edges, not top-k.

claim: Graph Machine scores 86.0% on Sudoku vs 71.7% for a same-scale Transformer
quote: GM 1 × Each Node, edge 2.70 M 86.0 ± 3.7
notes: Fixed-size Sudoku, no size extrapolation; 2.70M vs 2.12M params (not param-matched); Transformer-sin-PE-2x with ~8x params reaches 86.3.

claim: Graph Machine tests top-s address sparsity only in preliminary, dense-simulated experiments
quote: We conduct preliminary experiments on address sparsity by varying sparsity s , simulated using our dense algorithm and representation by masking non-top- s entries to 0 along the last dimension of edge addresses.

claim: Graph Machine frames itself as filling the gap between dense-dynamic Transformers and fixed-routing sparse Transformers
quote: In contrast to vanilla Transformers with dynamic dense interactions and sparse Transformers with fixed routing, a sparse Graph Machine would provide sparse but dynamic attention.
notes: "would provide" — proposed, not built.

claim: Labovich (2026) states it is unclear whether looped Transformers extrapolate to harder problems by iterating more
quote: Whether looped transformers actually achieve this extrapolation remains unclear.

claim: Labovich trains single-layer looped Transformers on chess, sudoku and prefix-sums, varying recall and normalisation (dense attention only)
quote: we train single-layer looped transformers on chess, sudoku, and prefix-sums and find that downstream performance tracks the framework’s predictions
notes: No sparse/top-k or entmax arm found.

claim: Plain TRM fails to extrapolate on A5 state tracking: 45.8% at length 128 after training on up to 32 updates
quote: plain TRM fails to extrapolate: at length 128, TRM and TRM with ACT enabled both obtain 45.8 % ± 3.9 % on A 5
notes: Trained up to 32 updates, tested up to 128.

claim: Adding a causal 1D convolution to TRM raises A5 length-128 accuracy to 91.4%
quote: Adding a causal 1D convolution layer substantially improves length generalization, reaching 91.4 % ± 2.3 % on A 5
notes: Locality prior, not learned sparse routing — a competitor explanation for extrapolation gains.

claim: Block Universal Transformer extrapolates to unseen recurrent depths on Rule 30 more reliably than CoTFormer, but degrades
quote: On Rule 30 cellular automata, BUT extrapolates to unseen recurrent depths more reliably than CoTFormer, although its accuracy eventually degrades.
notes: Dense attention; depth extrapolation, no sparse arm.

claim: Ray Chowdhury & Caragea suggest dense softmax noise in longer contexts may harm Universal Transformer length generalization
quote: higher noise from dense softmax in longer contexts may still harm its length generalization
notes: Hypothesis offered, not tested with a sparse arm; supports the dispersion motivation.

claim: Chunk-wise recurrence with a fixed attention window is more robust than depth-wise (UT) recurrence for length generalization
quote: chunk-wise recurrence with its fixed recurrent attention window tends to show more robustness than depth-wise recurrence in length generalization and flip-flop language modeling
notes: Fixed (not learned) sparsity; TMLR-era study; no top-k arm.

claim: Golowich et al.: length generalization occurs when each predicted token depends on a small fixed number of previous tokens
quote: Conceptually, we show that length generalization occurs as long as each predicted token depends on a small (fixed) number of previous tokens.
notes: Theory for an idealised sparse-attention hypothesis class; not looped; motivates k-sparse routing for extrapolation.

claim: Golowich et al. formalise k-sparse planted correlation distributions on which idealised transformers length-generalize
quote: We formalize such tasks via a notion we call k -sparse planted correlation distributions, and show that an idealized model of transformers which generalize attention heads successfully length-generalize on such tasks.

claim: Vanishing variance: layer norm after attention outputs improves length generalization on argmax retrieval and dictionary lookup
quote: On the argmax retrieval and dictionary lookup tasks, our experiments show that applying layer normalization after the attention outputs leads to significantly better length generalization.
notes: A third non-graph fix for dispersion (besides temperature and entmax) a reviewer may ask for.

claim: Sparsemax and alpha-entmax attention correspond to compact-kernel (e.g. Epanechnikov) Nadaraya-Watson regression; top-k is a heuristic within this family
quote: This unified perspective explains how sparsity naturally emerges from kernel design and provides principled alternatives to heuristic top- attention and other associative memory mechanisms.
notes: "top-k" symbol stripped in HTML extraction ("top- attention").

claim: Rectified-polynomial (alpha-entmax) kernels generalize strongly on MQMTAR length-generalization tasks in Memory Mosaics
quote: In contrast, our rectified polynomial kernels ( -entmax) exhibit strong and stable generalization, particularly on the MQMTAR task.
notes: Non-looped; adds evidence that sharpened attention is the baseline to beat.

claim: For top-k truncation of a softmax distribution, total-variation distance equals the discarded tail mass
quote: For a single attention distribution and its Top- truncation , we show that the total-variation distance coincides with the discarded softmax tail mass
notes: Gives the exact error of top-k vs dense softmax per step; useful for bounding the dense-vs-top-k gap per loop.

claim: Grouped Cross Attention learns end-to-end to retrieve top-k past chunks and reports length generalization far beyond pretraining context
quote: our key innovation allows the retriever to learn how to retrieve past chunks that better minimize the auto-regressive loss of subsequent tokens in an end-to-end manner.
notes: Learned unsupervised (by LM loss) top-k chunk retrieval; not looped; LM passkey only.

claim: Discrete Transformer uses hard attention strictly as an information-routing operator, discretised by temperature-annealed sampling
quote: we employ a hard attention mechanism designed strictly as an information routing operator, rather than a feature mixer.
notes: Algorithm-extraction focus; not looped; no extrapolation comparison vs dense.

claim: Sparse layers in looped LMs means top-k MoE FFNs (routing over experts), not sparse attention over tokens
quote: Replace dense FFNs with top-k MoE layers in looped LMs.
notes: Vocabulary trap: "sparse looped" hits are mostly MoE, not token routing.

claim: Foil (looped MoE) ends 0.012 nat below the unflattened looped baseline at equal parameters and compute
quote: the most flattened Foil ending 0.012 nat below the baseline at equal parameters and compute
notes: Expert routing, not token routing; LM only.

claim: Gated Recurrent Transformer: a 3-layer recurrent model matches a 12-layer GPT-2 Small under an iso-FLOPs constraint
quote: Under an iso FLOPs constraint, a 3-layer Gated Recurrent Transformer matches the accuracy of a 12-layer GPT-2 Small baseline with similar training and inference FLOPs
notes: Dense attention; LM; example of iso-FLOP looped evaluation protocol.

claim: Length-generalizable softmax CoT transformers are Turing-complete (via CoT C-RASP)
quote: we prove a stronger result that length-generalizable softmax CoT transformers are Turing-complete.
notes: Hard attention not required for this expressivity result; CoT, not looped.

claim: MiTA gathers top-k attended key-value pairs via landmark queries as routed experts
quote: which employs a small set of landmark queries to gather top- attended key-value pairs as query-aware and deformable routed experts
notes: Vision; non-looped; "top-k" symbol stripped in extraction.

claim: Persistent fast-slow latent recurrence improves OOD length generalization over recurrent, SSM and Transformer baselines
quote: Across these settings, persistent latent recurrence improves OOD generalization over recurrent, state-space, and Transformer baselines.
notes: Streaming recurrence, no sparse routing arm.

claim: Fast-slow recurrence ablations single out state-dependent transitions and feature-wise nonlinear mixing for OOD performance
quote: we identify architectural ingredients that are consistently associated with strong OOD performance, including state-dependent transitions and feature-wise nonlinear mixing.
